did_you_know.text: Did you know? David concluded that continuing to flee within Israel was dangerous, so he decided to move to the land of the Philistines, hoping that Saul would stop searching for him there.
Did you know? David did not go to Gath alone: he left with six hundred men, and their families later joined them.
Did you know? While he was staying in Gath, David had two wives: Ahinoam of Jezreel and Abigail, who had been the wife of Nabal the Carmelite.
Did you know? As soon as Saul heard that David had fled to Gath, he stopped pursuing him within Israel's borders.
Did you know? David asked Achish for a place to live outside Gath because he did not want his men living in the Philistine royal city alongside the king.
Did you know? Achish gave David Ziklag. The text adds that Ziklag has remained the property of the kings of Judah to this day.
Did you know? David lived in Philistine territory for a year and four months—a relatively long period during which he lived under Achish's protection.
Did you know? David and his men raided the Geshurites, the Girzites, and the Amalekites, who lived in the southern region extending toward the land of Egypt.
Did you know? After the raids, David took livestock and clothing as plunder—including sheep, cattle, donkeys, camels, and garments—and returned with it to Achish.

Did you know? When Achish asked David where he had raided, David replied as though he had acted in the Negev of Judah, the Negev of the Jerahmeelites, and the Negev of the Kenites, thereby concealing his actual targets.
Did you know? David left no man or woman alive in the places he raided, so that they could not reach Gath and tell Achish the truth about his actions.
Did you know? Achish believed that David had made himself hated by his own people, Israel, and therefore thought that David would remain his servant forever.
